content: SARIF 2.1.0 core spec (OASIS, cross-checked against GitHub code-scanning docs) defines webRequest (sec 3.46) and webResponse (sec 3.47) as first-class Result properties for DAST/web-analysis tools -- protocol/method/headers/body on the request side, statusCode/headers/body on the response side. These are core object model, not an extension. But GitHub code-scanning's ingestion path ignores them entirely: it requires physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri + region.startLine/endLine/startColumn/endColumn resolvable to a real repo file, and partialFingerprints.primaryLocationLineHash for dedup. ZAP's SARIF exporter reconciles this by faking a physicalLocation (URL as uri, startLine=1, attack payload as snippet) while also populating the real webRequest/webResponse objects -- i.e. two audiences, two representations, in the same file.
